On Windows, MaiCord 0.5.x through 0.7.x install this update from Settings > Updates. If you're still on 0.4.0, follow the one-time manual steps in the [0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/releases/tag/v0.5.0). On Linux, the installer and tarball installs and the AppImage update from Settings > Updates, packages through your package manager, and the musl AppImage through AppImageUpdate.

### What's new

- **Go Live: share your screen.** Stream a screen or a window, with its sound, from the voice card or the call bar, and watch others' streams as before.
  - Encoded on your GPU and end-to-end encrypted, at Discord's resolutions and frame rates up to your Nitro's or the server's boost tier. Turn on "Unlock all qualities" in the stream options to pick any of them, 1440p 60 fps included (off by default; only clients check these limits).
  - Stream modes (smoother video, clearer text, custom), mute stream audio, hide the preview, your own tile with its viewer list, and a stream menu to change the source or quality while live.
  - Light on the machine: nothing is encoded until someone watches, and a watched 1440p60 AV1 stream took about 12% of an AMD GPU's video engine in our tests, against 16% for the official client on the same settings.
  - On Windows, pick an application or a whole screen; on Linux, the desktop's share dialog opens. Sharing sound needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later, or PipeWire with xdg-desktop-portal on Linux. MaiCord's own sound is never shared.
- **Tabs in the title bar.** Turn them on in Settings > Appearance > Layout > "Show tabs in the title bar".
  - Pin channels and DMs with "+", Ctrl+T, a middle-click or "Open in new tab". Ctrl+Tab switches, Ctrl+W closes, Ctrl+1 to 9 jump; drag to reorder. An unread channel's tab shows a dot, and tabs come back after a restart.
  - "Open in new tab" on a picture, GIF, video, audio file or voice message gives it a page of its own. Videos and tracks keep playing while you work in another tab; a playlist gets a queue with thumbnails beside the player. Tabs and pages follow your theme, gradients included.
- **Account and server settings.** My Account (username, e-mail, phone, password, authenticator app, SMS, backup codes, security keys, disable and delete), Devices, Data and Privacy, Connected Apps, and blocked and ignored lists.
  - Servers gain a banner upload, Server Tag, Server Template, join applications, Enable Community and Integrations (command permissions, AutoMod, webhooks).
  - Accessibility follows Discord's: a live preview, UI density, chat text size, zoom (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0), saturation, role colour dots, underlined links and reduced motion. Streamer Mode hides invites and personal information, has a keybind, can switch on while OBS or XSplit runs, and on Windows keeps the window out of screen captures. Settings > Keybinds lists your custom keybinds.
- **Profiles, friends and Home**, laid out like Discord's: Board, Activity, Mutual Friends and Mutual Servers, connected accounts, a "Find or start a conversation" bar, Online, All, Pending and Add Friend, and Message Requests.
- **Chat.**
  - Select text across messages: a drag runs on over other messages and authors, scrolling the chat at the edges, and Ctrl+C copies them in order.
  - Type `@game` to mention a game; it shows as a chip and opens the game's profile.
  - Animated WebP images, like an X post's "GIF", get the favourite star, and favourites are saved as the official client saves them.
  - The free upload limit is 20 MiB, and Discord, not MaiCord, decides when a file is too large.
- **Voice.** Voice, stream audio, voice messages and the soundboard run on MaiCord's own Opus encoder and decoder: 26 to 32% less encoding time and 13 to 26% less decoding time than before, the same output on Windows and Linux, and it passes the Opus conformance vectors.

### Faster and smaller

- The Windows MaiCord.exe is 6.46 MB and the Linux program 6.47 MB, both under 6.5 MB with all of the above.
- The emoji picker scrolls on about a third of the GPU time (7 to 10% down to about 3% at 1440p), with no frame over 16.7 ms. Text rasterizes in 20% less GPU time, and WebM (VP8) video decodes in up to 27% less.
- Scrolling, switching channels and the member list use the same main-thread CPU time as 0.7.0 or less; deciding what to redraw takes 29% less time, and nothing wakes while the window is hidden.

### Fixed in this release

- A channel whose loaded messages didn't fill the window, such as a welcome channel of join messages, never loaded older ones, because there was nothing to scroll. MaiCord now loads older messages until the window is full, and the mouse wheel at the top always asks for more.
- A server could turn into a blank, unavailable icon if MaiCord received it while you were in one of its voice channels; it loads now.
- A 1440p stream or camera showed black in a large call tile; it shows at full size now.
- With a gradient theme, the taskbar and tray icon was Discord's blurple; it takes the theme's accent now.
- Some WebP avatars showed as a grey circle, and some GIFs failed to play; both work now.
- Moving the pointer over and off GIFs no longer cancels and resends the favourites download each time.
- Emoji suggestions after ":" rank by your use from the first message. Mention pills centre on their text.
- Screen readers get a heading and status on every sign-in screen.
- A crash when adding members to an integration, and settings text that could vanish after a failed rebuild.

### Removed

- Spotify sign-in (it saved a login nothing used); a saved one is deleted at startup. Spotify embeds, activity links and the profile connection are unchanged.
